help_text: Select one primary instrument from the lab inventory CSV. The chosen price contributes directly to the fixed-cost score.
Choose the chromatography column family and the exact column used. The selected column price contributes to the fixed-cost score.
Use the Auxiliary Equipment checklist below to capture pretreatment infrastructure costs.
This section covers the analytical mobile phase composition and per-run consumables cost.

text: What are the analytical consumables costs per run?
help_text: Enter total run time and flow rate, then choose solvents and buffers. Total analytical consumables cost = run time × flow rate × (solvent cost + buffer cost).
This section covers the sample pretreatment equipment used before the analytical step.
Select solvents used in sample pretreatment and enter volume in mL per sample for each selected solvent.
Select reagents used in sample pretreatment and enter weight in g per sample for each selected reagent.
Select sample preparation materials and enter quantity per sample for each selected item.
Enter the number of analytes in the method. This is used for the analytical performance summary and practical reporting.
Enter the Limit of Quantification. Lower is better. Scoring: <1 = Excellent, <3 = Good, <10 = Acceptable, >10 = Poor.

text: Enter number of peaks with Rs < 1.5 (including admixtures)
help_text: Enter the number of peaks with resolution below 1.5. Scoring: 0 = Excellent, 1 = Good, 2 = Acceptable, >3 = Poor.

text: What is the Precision of your method (RSD%)?
help_text: Enter the RSD%. Scoring: <2.5% = Excellent, <3.5% = Good, <5% = Acceptable, >5% = Poor.

text: What is the Repeatability of your method (RSD%)?
help_text: Enter the RSD%. Scoring: <2% = Excellent, <3% = Good, <5% = Acceptable, >5% = Poor.

text: What is the Accuracy of your method (% error in standard solution)?
help_text: Enter the % error. Scoring: <1.5% = Excellent, <2% = Good, <3.5% = Acceptable, >3.5% = Poor.

text: What is the Recovery of your assay (% error)?
help_text: Enter the % error. Scoring: <3% = Excellent, <4% = Good, <5% = Acceptable, >5% = Poor.

text: What is the Linearity (r²) of your method?
help_text: Enter the r² value (e.g. 0.9991). Scoring: ≥0.999 = Excellent, ≥0.998 = Good, ≥0.997 = Acceptable, <0.997 = Poor.

text: Enter the retention factor (k) of the first analyte
help_text: Enter the k value. Scoring: 2-3 = Excellent, 3-6 = Good, 6-10 or 1.5-2 = Acceptable, outside 1-10 = Poor.
Enter the Tf value. Scoring: 0.8-1.2 = Excellent, 0.7-1.5 = Good, 0.6-2 = Acceptable, outside = Poor.

text: Enter the number of theoretical plates (N)
help_text: Enter the N value. Scoring: >4000 = Excellent, >2000 = Good, >1000 = Acceptable, <1000 = Poor.
Indicate whether carry-over has been evaluated for your method.

text: Robustness: number of parameters that remained robust after testing
help_text: Enter the number of parameters that remained robust after testing. Scoring: >5 = Excellent, >4 = Good, >3 = Acceptable, ≤2 = Poor.
Sample analysis results for the matrix and substrate type.
Select the substrate challenge level for the analysed sample type. Values are sourced from the sample-analysis-results CSV file.
Enter the matrix recovery as a percentage. Higher values indicate better recovery from the matrix.
Enter the matrix effect as a percentage. Values closer to 100% are usually preferred.
% process efficiency = matrix recovery × matrix effect. Enter the resulting percentage value.

text: Enter reliable detection limit in matrix (µg/mL)
help_text: Enter the reliable detection limit in matrix. For industrial methods use µg/mL and for advanced methods use ng/mL.

text: Number of analytes covered by the method
help_text: Enter the number of analytes. Value will auto-populate from analytical performance section. Scoring: >4 = Excellent, 3 = Good, 2 = Acceptable, 1 = Poor.

text: How many samples can be simultaneously pretreated? (Enter 11 if no pretreatment is needed)
help_text: Enter the number of simultaneous samples. Scoring: >10 = Excellent, >6 = Good, >2 = Acceptable, 1 = Poor.

text: Total analysis time including recalibration (gradient elution), in minutes
help_text: Enter the time in minutes. Value will auto-populate from analytical performance section. Scoring: <5 = Excellent, <10 = Good, <20 = Acceptable, >20 = Poor.
Enter the pretreatment time. Scoring: <15 = Excellent, <30 = Good, <45 = Acceptable, >45 = Poor.

text: Is plastic used in the pretreatment procedure?
help_text: Select the level of plastic use in your pretreatment procedure.

text: What is the Hazard score for your method? (NFPA score × mL for both analysis and pretreatment)
help_text: Multiply the NFPA hazard score by the total mL used. Scoring: <5 = Excellent, <15 = Good, <25 = Acceptable, >25 = Poor.
